searchText: I've noticed some small dips in participation every so often from 96% -> 99% they only last an epoch or so https://cdn.discordapp.com/attachments/476588476393848832/786830940931358730/unknown.png I'm not sure if it's some operation restarting their nodes or something more interesting Could be that epoch transition which is more resource intensive throws some weaker validators off. it's interesting because of how consistent it is I'll look into it over the weekend and report back zooming into one of these "dips" you can see issues voting on the correct head/target I don't think this is a _large_ operation taking their nodes offline I think I may have found an example: https://beaconcha.in/block/73816 the epoch that this block is in has 96% participation, and this block only has 3 votes while all other blocks in this epoch have ~>1k votes given that there are 32 slots per epoch, one bad block could drop the participation by 1/32 ~= 3% we're seeing the theory being high propagation latency so that validators in that slot broadcast an attestation w the incorrect head, but ultimately the "late" block is included in the canonical chain this would explain the dip in "incorrect head" but does not explain the dip in "incorrect target" this particular block is 26/32 slots into the epoch so *should* be plenty of time for the boundary block to have propagated hmm. I'm not sure how this voting participation is calculated, but here's an example I found that correlates with ^ https://beaconcha.in/block/63776 the epoch for this block has 99%, but the next epoch has 96%. this is the last block in the epoch seeing the same thing on my graphs for this one - incorrect head and target votes <@!203220829473996800> https://hackmd.io/@potuz/SyU-uNZnv My whole family decided to fall ill today so I doubt I'll interpret more those numbers for a couple of days. Will update though with newer data in a couple of days. I'm no blogger so don't expect fancy writing, but I'm sure smart people here can take something out of this. There is a systematic error here which is that I am assuming that my node is in the canonical chainhead. This is perfect in mainnet, and has been on target on pyrmont as far as I have been checking. But I am not constantly checking this assumption during data gathering. Mostly cause I don't have time to change the script. <@!124259917560414210> <@!539495253418180618> This is related to what you are discussing very insightful, thanks for sharing <@!755590043632140352> You're awesome, thanks for looking into this. Take care of family first, we'll get to these eth2 performance things later.
